Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate dextrocardia (heart apex pointing to the right) and gastric bubble on the right side, indicating situs inversus totalis. Additionally, there are increased markings and tram-line opacities at the lung bases consistent with bronchiectasis. This triad of situs inversus, bronchiectasis, and sinusitis (implied by the syndrome name) is characteristic of Kartagener’s syndrome.
